content_preview.title: Historic Heat Wave Pushes PJM Grid to the Brink of a 20-Year Demand Record, Prompting Emergency DOE Orders
content_preview.summary: A brutal early-July heat wave pushed PJM's forecast demand to 166.3 GW, threatening the grid's 165,563 MW record from 2006, as DOE ordered emergency fossil-fuel dispatch and data-center curtailment.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

An early-July heat wave pushed electricity demand on PJM Interconnection, the nation's largest grid operator, to within reach of a 20-year-old record, according to [Reuters](https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/warnings-galore-as-largest-us-power-grid-braces-for-record-demand-4770933). Demand on the 13-state grid topped 160 gigawatts on Wednesday, July 1, and was forecast to hit 166.3 gigawatts around 6 p.m. EDT on Thursday, July 2 — enough to break PJM's all-time record...

editor_notes.source_verification: All 4 sources personally verified. (1) sources/2026-07/historic-heat-wave-pushes-pjm-grid-to-the-brink-of-a-20-year-demand-record-prompting-emergency-doe-orders/source-1.html.gz (Utility Dive, HTTP 200, sha256 verified 4a21c49a...): confirms the 165,563 MW 2006 record, the verbatim quote 'direct transmission owners, if required as a last resort prior to voltage reduction or load shed, to curtail data centers and other large loads that have backup generation,' the verbatim quote 'authorizing only the necessary additional generation on the conditions contained in this Order,' NYISO's 32,410 MW Thursday peak forecast, ISO New England's 25,850 MW ~7pm forecast, the 115-degree heat index, and the 167,000 outages Tuesday night. (2) source-2.html.gz (energy.gov 'Energy Secretary Secures Mid-Atlantic Grid...', HTTP 200, sha256 verified 600517f4...): confirms the June 27/29 application dates, the two-order structure, the verbatim Wright quote 'Maintaining affordable, reliable, and secure power in the PJM service territory is non-negotiable,' the EEA-3 (top-tier Energy Emergency Alert) framing, and the June 30 11:59pm-July 3 11:59pm EDT effective window. (3) source-3.html.gz (energy.gov Section 202(c) order docket, HTTP 200, sha256 verified 76e664c2...): confirms Order No. 202-26-32 and its dispatch directive, and the extension as Order No. 202-26-32A effective July 2 through July 6 11:59pm EDT. (4) https://www.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/warnings-galore-as-largest-us-power-grid-braces-for-record-demand-4770933 (Reuters wire piece by Tim McLaughlin, dateline BOSTON, July 1, republished on investing.com, which is on config/source_allowlist.txt) returned HTTP 403 to the automated snapshot fetcher (bot-blocked) and has no local snapshot (file: null in manifest.json). Per the skill's last-resort fallback, I WebFetched the live URL directly and confirmed it verbatim supports every claim attributed to it: the 160 GW Wednesday demand, the 166.3 GW Thursday 6pm forecast against the 165.5 GW 2006 record, the Virginia-zone wholesale price surge past $600/MWh, coal generation up to 22% of supply / ~28 GW / ~75% above 2026 average, PJM's 18 GW of 30-minute reserve resources, and MISO's 127.1 GW existing record. This source is verified accurate; only its provenance snapshot is missing due to bot-blocking, not its content.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: One misattribution found: the first 'What We Know' bullet states 'PJM, which delivers power to 67 million people across 13 states and Washington, D.C. ... according to Utility Dive.' The cited Utility Dive snapshot contains no population or state-count figure anywhere in its text (verified by keyword search — zero matches for 'million' or '13 states'). The underlying fact is true and independently verifiable (PJM's own territory page confirms 13 states + D.C.; reputable secondary sources cite PJM's service population at 65-67 million depending on the year), but it is not supported by the source cited in the article. This is a citation error on a true fact, not a fabrication, and it sits in a subordinate 'What We Know' bullet rather than the headline, summary, or Overview lead — the headline, summary, and lead paragraph all trace cleanly to Utility Dive/Reuters/DOE sources that were verified. All other specifics (demand figures, prices, DOE order numbers and dates, all direct quotes) trace correctly to their cited sources with no other discrepancies found.
